Randomly-stopped sums

Source: vignettes/randomlyStoppedSumCGF.Rmd
randomlyStoppedSumCGF.Rmd

This vignette explains how to build and use a CGF for a randomly-stopped sum with randomlyStoppedSumCGF(), and (most importantly) how to avoid the most common replication/blocking mistakes.

Model

A randomly-stopped sum has the form

Y=∑i=1NXi, Y = \sum_{i=1}^{N} X_i,

where

  • NN is a scalar non-negative integer count random variable,
  • X1,X2,…X_1,X_2,\dots are i.i.d. copies of a (possibly vector-valued) random vector XX,
  • NN is independent of all XiX_i.

In CGF terms, the key identity is the composition

KY(t;θ)=KN(KX(t;θ);θ), K_Y(t;\theta) = K_N\bigl( K_X(t;\theta);\theta \bigr),

where KX(t;θ)K_X(t;\theta) is a scalar even when tt is a vector.

You provide:

  • count_cgf: a CGF for NN (scalar),
  • summand_cgf: a CGF for XX (scalar or vector),
  • a shared parameter vector theta (both CGFs read from the same theta).

library(saddlepoint)

The one thing to get right: block_size and iidReps

Many CGFs in this package are vectorized and can interpret a long tvec in more than one way. For RSS models that ambiguity can silently change the statistical model (scalar vs vector, “one observation” vs “many i.i.d. observations”).

randomlyStoppedSumCGF() forces you to disambiguate:

  • block_size = dimension of one observation YbY_b (equals dim of the summand XX).
  • iidReps = number of i.i.d. observations BB in your dataset.

Recommended patterns

Scalar RSS data (a numeric vector y of length B):

  • safest: specify block_size = 1 and let iidReps = "any" (defaulted internally).

cg_rss <- randomlyStoppedSumCGF(count_cgf   = PoissonCGF,
                                summand_cgf = BinomialModelCGF(n = adaptor(fixed_param = 1),
                                                               prob = adaptor(fixed_param = 0.3)), 
                                block_size  = 1)

Vector RSS data (each observation is length d, stored as a d x B matrix):

  • set block_size = d,
  • either set iidReps = "any" (and let it infer B from length(tvec) / d) or set iidReps = B.

What happens if you get it wrong?

If you forget block_size / iidReps, a “long” tvec might be treated as:

  • a higher-dimensional summand XX, which changes the model for YY, or
  • multiple i.i.d. blocks in some child CGF (again changing KX(t)K_X(t), hence changing KY(t)K_Y(t)).

That is why RSS requires at least one of block_size or iidReps.

Example 1: Poisson count + Bernoulli summand = Poisson thinning (closed form)

Let

  • N∼Poisson(λ)N \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda),
  • X∼Bernoulli(p)X \sim \text{Bernoulli}(p), i.i.d.,
  • Y=∑i=1NXiY = \sum_{i=1}^N X_i.

Then Y∼Poisson(λp)Y \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda p) (Poisson thinning), so the RSS CGF should match a Poisson CGF with mean λp\lambda p.


lambda <- 4
p      <- 0.3
theta  <- c(lambda = lambda, p = p)

cg_N <- PoissonModelCGF(lambda = adaptor(indices = 1))
cg_X <- BinomialModelCGF(n = adaptor(fixed_param = 1), prob = adaptor(indices = 2))

cg_rss <- randomlyStoppedSumCGF(count_cgf   = cg_N,
                               summand_cgf = cg_X,
                               block_size  = 1) # scalar Y

tt <- c(-0.2, 0.1, 0.05)

# RSS CGF:
K_rss <- cg_rss$K(tt, theta)

# Closed-form equivalent:
K_closed <- PoissonCGF$K(tt, lambda * p)

cbind(K_rss, K_closed)
#>            K_rss    K_closed
#> [1,] -0.02979268 -0.02979268
stopifnot(all.equal(K_rss, K_closed, tol = 1e-12))

Example 2: Poisson count + categorical summand = Poisson splitting (vector, closed form)

Let

  • N∼Poisson(λ)N \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda),
  • XX is a ‘one-hot’ vector in {e1,…,ed}\{e_1,\dots,e_d\} with probabilities π\pi,
  • Y=∑i=1NXiY = \sum_{i=1}^N X_i is a vector of category counts.

Then the components of YY are independent Poisson with means λπj\lambda \pi_j.


set.seed(1)
d <- 3
lambda <- 10
pi_ <- c(0.2, 0.5, 0.3)
theta <- c(lambda = lambda, pi_)

cg_N <- PoissonModelCGF(lambda = adaptor(indices = 1), iidReps = 1)

# summand: Multinomial with n=1 gives a categorical one-hot vector
cg_X <- MultinomialModelCGF(
  n = adaptor(fixed_param = 1),
  prob_vec = adaptor(indices = 2:(d+1)),
  iidReps = 1
)

cg_rss_vec <- randomlyStoppedSumCGF(cg_N, cg_X, block_size = d)

# Check K1 at t=0 equals E[Y] = lambda * pi_
cg_rss_vec$K1(rep(0, d), theta)
#> [1] 2 5 3
lambda * pi_
#> [1] 2 5 3

Example 3: Compound Poisson–Gamma

A classic ‘not-nicely-closed-form’ RSS is the compound Poisson–Gamma:

  • N∼Poisson(λ)N \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda),
  • X∼Gamma(α,β)X \sim \text{Gamma}(\alpha,\beta) i.i.d. severities (shape α\alpha, rate β\beta),
  • Y=∑i=1NXiY = \sum_{i=1}^N X_i.

The distribution of YY has a point mass at 0 and a continuous density for y>0y>0. The exact density is an infinite series fY(y)=e−λ∑k=1∞λkk!fΓ(y;kα,β), f_Y(y) = e^{-\lambda}\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\frac{\lambda^k}{k!} f_{\Gamma}(y;\,k\alpha,\beta), so in practice “exact” likelihood evaluation typically needs truncation or special-purpose methods.

This is a good use case for saddlepoint likelihoods.

Build the RSS CGF 


set.seed(123)

alpha_fix <- 2
theta_true <- c(lambda = 10, rate = 3)

cg_N <- PoissonModelCGF(lambda = adaptor(indices = 1) ) # optional # iidReps = 1
cg_X <- GammaModelCGF(shape = adaptor(fixed_param = alpha_fix),
                      rate  = adaptor(indices = 2)) # optional # iidReps = 1

cg_rss <- randomlyStoppedSumCGF(cg_N, cg_X, block_size = 1)

Simulate data 


B <- 100
Y <- cg_rss$rsim(iidReps = B, parameter_vector = theta_true)
summary(Y)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>   1.099   4.856   5.988   6.183   7.644  11.917

Fit via saddlepoint likelihood 


fit_spa <- find.saddlepoint.MLE(
  observed.data  = Y,
  cgf            = cg_rss,  # iidReps="any" because we supplied block_size=1
  starting.theta = c(2, 1),
  lb.theta       = c(1e-3, 1e-6),
  method         = "constrained",  # usually safest when there are domain constraints
  std.error      = TRUE,
  discrepancy = TRUE
)

fit_spa$MLEs.theta
#> [1] 10.208868  3.302203
fit_spa$std.error
#> [1] 1.4671329 0.4689042

Compare against an exact likelihood

The following uses the infinite-series density truncated at kmax.


d_comp_pois_gamma <- function(y, lambda, alpha, rate, kmax = 200) {
  if (y == 0) return(exp(-lambda))
  ks <- 1:kmax
  weights <- exp(-lambda) * lambda^ks / factorial(ks)
  dens <- dgamma(y, shape = ks * alpha, rate = rate)
  sum(weights * dens)
}

nll_trunc <- function(theta) {
  lam <- theta[1]; rate <- theta[2]
  -sum(log(vapply(Y, d_comp_pois_gamma, numeric(1),
                  lambda = lam, alpha = alpha_fix, rate = rate, kmax = 200)))
}

fit_trunc <- nlminb(
  start = c(1, 1),
  objective = nll_trunc,
  lower = c(1e-6, 1e-6)
)

rbind(true = theta_true, spa = fit_spa$MLEs.theta, true_mle = fit_trunc$par)
fit_spa$discrepancy                # approximated difference
fit_trunc$par - fit_spa$MLEs.theta # exact difference

Practical checklist

When using randomlyStoppedSumCGF():

  1. Always decide what one observation is.
    • If one observation is scalar, set block_size = 1.
    • If one observation is a vector of length d, set block_size = d.
  2. Decide how you store the data.
    • scalar data: observed.data as a vector of length B
    • vector data: observed.data as a d x B matrix (columns = i.i.d. blocks)
  3. If constraints exist, prefer method="constrained" in find.saddlepoint.MLE().
